docs.purpose: Once a day this job checks that the data pipelines actually ran recently and that a database backup actually happened, and turns the build red if either is missing. It is the alarm for silence: a pipeline that stops running produces no error of its own, so something has to go looking. If the backup is missing and no permit run is currently in flight, the watchdog takes a backup itself, then re-checks and only then decides whether to raise the alarm.
docs.data_story: It reads `pipeline_runs` and writes no table. It runs on `45 18 * * *`, unattended, with nobody watching — which is why its guard matters: an explicit environment guard step that fails the job when SUPABASE_DATABASE_URL is empty or the Supabase CA cert file is missing (a missing GitHub secret interpolates to an empty string and does not fail a workflow on its own); plus `concurrency.group: ${{ github.workflow }}` with cancel-in-progress: false, and a `migrate.js --verify` pre-flight run as `continue-on-error: true` with an end-of-job escalation gate.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **JOB descriptor** of archetype `SCHEDULED` under its own `job.schema.json` (Spec 128 R-14) — declaring its schedule, its target, its idempotency posture, its behaviour when `pg_cron` is absent, and the audit row it writes. Nothing about how it runs changes; what changes is that those five answers stop living only in SQL and YAML.

contracts: none — a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow takes no request and calls no API route

spec_refs: docs/specs/01-pipeline/118_deep_scrapes_execution_envelope.md §2 (the two-red geometry that moved the cron)

versioning.why: Its exit-code choreography, its cron slot and its freshness constants are all pinned by two test files in both directions — the cron must fire at or after 18:30 UTC, the redirects must stay absent, and BACKUP_SLUGS must equal exactly the two shapes.

inputs.why: It reads exactly one table, pipeline_runs, asking two absence questions: has each applicable chain landed a RAN_STATUSES row inside its own window, and has a backup row landed inside 25h. No contract, no parameter.

evidence: scripts/lib/step/ledger.js:62 — the only INSERT into this table

outputs.why: MEASURED: it writes nothing to any table. check-pipeline-freshness.js builds its own Pool and only SELECTs; the backup fallback runs scripts/backup-db.js, which is a legacy pipeline.run() script — and scripts/lib/pipeline.js's run() contains no pipeline_runs insert at all (the only INSERT in the SDK is scripts/lib/step/ledger.js:62, which backup-db.js does not use). Its output is an S3 object plus $GITHUB_OUTPUT lines.

state.why: Three booleans passed between steps through $GITHUB_OUTPUT (chains_fresh, backup_fresh, permits_running) and nothing else; the script is invoked twice and shares no state between the two runs.

staleness.why: It renders nothing. What it MEASURES is staleness — its own windows are 25h for chain_coa/chain_permits/backup, 26h for chain_entities, 204h for chain_sources and 33h/83h weekday-aware for chain_deep_scrapes.

session.why: NOT ANSWERABLE from the closed set: guards.session offers anon | authenticated | entitled | admin, all of which describe an end-user principal. This runs with no request and no user — as the pg_cron job owner through a SECURITY DEFINER function, or as a GitHub Actions runner holding repository secrets. Spec 128 §4 escalation (Spec 128 R-14 already anticipates JOBs getting their own job.schema.json); recorded rather than mis-answered.

rls_class.why: pipeline_runs is named in the catalog's representative Class B list; the workflow connects with SUPABASE_DATABASE_URL, a service credential, not an end-user role.

checks.why: Only the FINAL freshness check determines the job conclusion — the first carries continue-on-error so the backup fallback can still run, and losing that asymmetry turns a recoverable staleness into a hard red before the safety net fires.

A stale chain is exactly when the backup safety net matters most; the chains_fresh term that used to gate the fallback suppressed it during the live 2026-08-03 incident (backups 50.7h stale against a 25h SLA).
An in-flight permits chain may complete its own backup_db step moments later; without the permits_running guard a concurrent direct invocation double-runs the backup.

MEASURED FAILING: BACKUP_SLUGS is asserted to be exactly {backup_db, permits:backup_db} (check-pipeline-freshness.logic.test.ts:48-51), but the fallback invocation writes NO pipeline_runs row under either slug — pipeline.run() has no ledger insert — so the re-check after a successful fallback still reads backup_fresh=false.

The script self-writes its $GITHUB_OUTPUT lines; a >> redirect on the step swallowed stdout including the ::error annotations naming WHICH chain was stale, and the 2026-07-31 red run needed log archaeology because of it.

errors.why: It has no error UI and no envelope: a DB-check failure is fail-loud (exit 1 with all three outputs false), and an unreachable database during a freshness check is itself the outage signal.

emits.why: It writes no pipeline_runs row of its own, so the watchdog's own liveness is unobservable from the house observability surface — the same structural blind spot it exists to close for the chains.

offers.why: A CI workflow renders no sponsored placement.

config.why: Every threshold is a JavaScript constant in check-pipeline-freshness.js — FRESHNESS_WINDOW_HOURS 25, CHAIN_WINDOWS_HOURS, and deepScrapesWindow's 33/83 — not a registered logic variable; they are pinned by tests instead.

sharing.why: It renders no contract. pipeline_runs is read by other surfaces (the admin stats route, FreshnessTimeline) but that is a shared TABLE, not a shared contract of this job.

limitations.what: The Spec 112 §6 backup fallback cannot satisfy the freshness re-check that follows it.
limitations.measured: scripts/backup-db.js:26,122 uses pipeline.run() from scripts/lib/pipeline.js, whose run() (575-611) performs no pipeline_runs insert; the only SDK insert is scripts/lib/step/ledger.js:62, which backup-db.js does not use. BACKUP_SLUGS (check-pipeline-freshness.js:109) therefore matches nothing the fallback writes, and check-pipeline-freshness.js:20-25 claims the standalone backup_db row IS written by this invocation — a comment the tree contradicts.

limitations.what: The watchdog cannot detect its own absence.
limitations.measured: It writes no pipeline_runs row (scripts/check-pipeline-freshness.js:1-10 — a standalone CLI, not a pipeline.run() step), so a workflow that stops triggering is invisible in exactly the way it exists to make chain absence visible.

limitations.what: chain_sources is checked with a 204h window against a chain that is disabled.
limitations.measured: scripts/check-pipeline-freshness.js:101-106 — the comment records chain_sources as disabled_manually pending Phase B B6, with the window left un-re-derived.

notes: The schedule is LIVE (the yml header records that an earlier comment claiming it was inert went stale and was corrected in the WF3 F5 fold, 2026-08-15, which also moved the cron 15:30 -> 18:45 UTC). writes_tables is measured-EMPTY, not unknown: scripts/check-pipeline-freshness.js only SELECTs from pipeline_runs (:193), and scripts/backup-db.js contains no INSERT/UPDATE at all and uses the legacy `pipeline.run()` SDK, which writes no ledger row itself (pipeline_runs inserts live in scripts/lib/step/ledger.js:62, not on this path) — so the fallback backup writes S3, not a DB table. The yml header's mention of 'a standalone backup_db slug' row shape is a read-side tolerance in the freshness query, not a write this job performs. MEASURED 2026-09-15, one finding worth a WF3. The Spec 112 §6 backup safety net writes no ledger row: backup-db.js:122 calls pipeline.run('backup-db', ...) from the LEGACY SDK (scripts/lib/pipeline.js:575-611), which opens a pool, runs the body and ends the pool — it contains no INSERT INTO pipeline_runs. The only ledger insert in the SDK is scripts/lib/step/ledger.js:62, reached through scripts/lib/step/index.js, which backup-db.js does not require (grep count 0 for "lib/step"). So after the fallback runs successfully, the final freshness re-check still finds no row under either BACKUP_SLUGS value and reddens the job. check-pipeline-freshness.js:20-25 states the opposite in a comment ("the standalone backup_db slug, written when this workflow invokes scripts/backup-db.js directly") — the brief's trap 3, live. Separately: the workflow passes PIPELINE_CHAIN=pipeline-watchdog to every step, which is the env var the CONVERTED-step SDK reads to decide ledger-row ownership (scripts/lib/step/index.js:3299-3306) — harmless for backup-db.js today only because it is on the legacy path. Filed here rather than fixed: this shard is a census, not a change.
